$S_0 = 0$.
$S_1 = c$.
$S_2 = c - c = 0$.
$S_3 = 0 + c = c$.
$S_4 = c - c = 0$.

Since $c > 0$, $c \pmod 1$ is a single point distinct from 0 unless $c$ is an integer (which is impossible since $c < 1$ must hold if we want the path to be potentially non-trivial, although the problem only requires $c>0$).
